title: Reorder List
statement:
You are given the `head` of a non-empty singly linked list `L0 → L1 → … → Ln-1 → Ln`.

Rearrange it **in place** so that it alternates between the front and the back:

`L0 → Ln → L1 → Ln-1 → L2 → Ln-2 → …`

Move the existing nodes by rewiring `next` pointers; don't change any node's `val`. The method returns nothing — the tests read the list starting from the `head` they passed in.

target.note: the benchmark time includes building the input list, which is also linear

hints: The new order takes nodes from the front going forward and from the back going backward. A singly linked list can't walk backward — how could you make the back half walk forward instead?
Split the list at the middle (slow/fast pointers), reverse the second half, and now you have two forward lists to interleave.

Find the middle so the first half has the extra node when the length is odd. Cut after the middle, reverse the second half in place, then alternate: take one node from the first list, one from the reversed second, until the second runs out.
followups: The easy way is to copy the nodes into an ArrayList and use two indices. What does that cost, and when is it the better choice?
How would you check whether a linked list is a palindrome in O(1) extra space? Which parts of this solution carry over?
Could you restore the original list afterwards?
explain: This is three classic linked-list moves chained together. First, slow/fast pointers find the middle: when fast can't take two more steps, slow is the last node of the first half. Second, cut there (slow.next = null — forgetting this makes a cycle) and reverse the second half in place. Third, weave: save both lists' next nodes, point a at b and b at a's old next, then advance. For n nodes the first half has ceil(n/2) and the reversed second half floor(n/2), so the weave stops when the second list runs out. Each step is linear: O(n) time, O(1) extra space. Copying the nodes into an ArrayList and pairing the ends is also O(n) but uses O(n) space; walking to the tail for every step is O(n^2).
